business: Almissa Digital: done-for-you AI guest assistant for holiday rentals, Omiš/Croatia
by_segment: Villa owner with pool (high-end, weekly bookings, often lives abroad or in Split)
Small portfolio host (2 to 6 units, renting is a main income)
Single-apartment family host (one unit in or next to the family house)
why_not: Booking and Airbnb already send my automatic messages for free, and I answer guests on WhatsApp myself. I'm not putting a robot between me and a German guest when one wrong answer about parking or check-in can turn a 9.5 into a 9.2.

My Booking score is my income, and I'm not letting a brand-new one-person company's robot talk to my guests. My laminated sheet has never given a wrong answer, and when guests write to me I answer them myself.

I have one apartment and Booking already sends my scheduled messages, and the house-rules sheet on the table answers the rest. On about eight thousand a year, €120 for something that answers the same three questions I already answer myself doesn't make sense.

I have one apartment right next to my house, so when a guest needs something they knock on my door or send me a WhatsApp and I answer. €120 is a lot of money for me to pay for something I already do myself for free.

Booking and Airbnb scheduled messages plus my printed house-rules sheet already answer the Wi-Fi and check-in questions. My guests pay a lot for the villa and they expect me, not a chatbot, so I don't see what this adds.

Answering my guests myself, even at midnight, is my hospitality and why they come back and leave good reviews. It is not expensive, but I don't want a machine talking to my guests in my name, and the Wi-Fi password is already on a card on the fridge.

My guests come back because they talk to me, Jasper, not to a machine. I already answer the Wi-Fi and parking questions myself on WhatsApp, and €120 a season is real money for something I do for free.

My guests pay a lot for a villa week and they get me, not a robot; answering them myself, even at midnight, is the hospitality. The price is nothing, but a QR card in my villa tells them I don't have time for them.

I have one apartment next to our house, and when guests have a question I'm right there or I answer on my phone at lunch. Booking and Airbnb already send my Wi-Fi and check-in messages for free, so €120 a season is money I'd rather keep.
why_yes: In July and August I can't answer the same Wi-Fi and pool questions at midnight from abroad, and €120 for the season is nothing next to one week's booking at the villa. If it catches the routine stuff and sends the real problems to my WhatsApp, it's worth trying, especially with the refund.
